name: Tasker: Task Actions
description: Composes one Tasker task from actions: the action list with codes and argument shapes, JavaScriptlet helpers (performTask, setLocal/local, global/setGlobal, flash, sendIntent, shell), Input and List Dialogs, HTTP Request, Perform Task with %par1/%par2 and a return variable, If/Goto flow, error handling (Continue Task After Error, %err/%errmsg), and calls into Termux (RUN_COMMAND) and Claude Code agents. Use it to write or fix a task body; use tasker-profile-builder for what triggers it, tasker-scene-xml for scene elements and the dialog/overlay gotchas, tasker-variables for scope and naming, tasker-project-architecture when the task does not yet have a place in a project. Pairs with: build-claude-agents.py and build-claude-panel.py (helper functions javascriptlet, input_dialog, list_dialog, wait_ms, goto_if_matches emit verified XML for codes 129, 360, 378, 30, 135), tasker-edit.py --add-tasks FILE.prj.xml PROJECT to add generated tasks to an existing project, tasker-import.sh for a new project, and the android-assistant run_tasker_task MCP tool to run the result by name. Related: termux-proot-bridge (the Termux side of RUN_COMMAND), termux-api-commands, phone-agent-handoff (shape of an agent's report), android-automation-router. Variables: task_name = the task's unique name, with its project prefix; purpose = what the task does, step by step if known; inputs = where its inputs come from (%par1/%par2, a dialog, %input from a profile, a file, nothing if started by run_tasker_task); outputs = what it must produce (Return value, notification, flash, file, a variable another task reads); external_calls = Termux scripts, Claude agents, HTTP endpoints or apps it calls.
content:
Write the Tasker task **{{task_name}}**.

## Purpose
{{purpose}}

## Inputs
{{inputs}}

## Outputs
{{outputs}}

## External calls
{{external_calls}}

## Building blocks

**Action codes verified on this phone (Tasker 6.7.6 exports and the build-claude-*.py generators)**
- 129 JavaScriptlet: Str arg0 code, Str arg1 libraries, Int arg2 auto-exit (1), Int arg3 timeout in seconds.
- 360 Input Dialog: arg1 title, arg2 text, arg3 default, Int arg4 timeout; the answer is in %input.
- 378 List Dialog: Int arg1 1 (single choice), arg2 title, arg3 items (a variable such as %my_items holding a comma-separated list), arg6 OK label, arg7 cancel label, Int arg9 timeout, Int arg10-12 0; the choice is in %ld_selected.
- 30 Wait: Int arg0 ms, arg1 s, arg2 min, arg3 h, arg4 days. Other tasks run meanwhile.
- 135 Goto: ConditionList (op 2 = matches, lhs, rhs) + Int arg0 0, Int arg1 target action number (1-based), Str arg2 label.
- 130 Perform Task: Str arg0 the task name (tasker-edit's reference check reads it there), then priority, %par1, %par2 and the return variable. Use a literal name: a name held in a variable cannot be checked and breaks silently when the task is renamed.
- 159 Profile Status, 47 Show Scene, 49 Destroy Scene, 51 Element Text (scenes: tasker-scene-xml).
For any other action (Variable Set, If/End If, HTTP Request, Notify, Run Shell, Return, Stop ...) do not guess the code or argument order: build the action once in Tasker's UI, export the task, and copy the shape.

**JavaScriptlet helpers** (Tasker's JS functions)
- `local('name')` / `setLocal('name', value)`: task-local variables, names without % and lowercase. Locals are also plain JS variables (`input`, `ld_selected`); test `typeof input !== 'undefined'` and that the value does not still start with '%' (an unset variable reads as its own name).
- `global('Name')` / `setGlobal('Name', value)`: globals.
- `performTask(name, priority, par1, par2)`: start another task by name.
- `flash(text)`: a short toast, the cheapest progress signal.
- `sendIntent(action, target, package, class, category, data, mime, extras)`: target 'service', 'receiver' or 'activity'; extras is an array of 'key:value' strings, so String extras only: a String[] extra such as RUN_COMMAND_ARGUMENTS cannot be passed this way, so use RUN_COMMAND_STDIN or a wrapper script.
- `shell(cmd, asRoot, timeoutSeconds)`: returns stdout with CRs dropped.
- Keep one JavaScriptlet to one short step. A long JS loop blocks other tasks: poll with JS + Wait (30) + Goto (135) instead.

**Dialogs**
Input Dialog for free text, List Dialog for a choice: fill the list variable in a JavaScriptlet with `setLocal('my_items', 'A,B,C')`, show 378 with arg3 `%my_items`, read the choice in the next JavaScriptlet with `local('ld_selected')`, and map labels to task names in a JS object (the "Ask AI" chooser in build-claude-agents.py). A scene shown as an overlay cancels dialogs: hide it first.

**HTTP**
Use HTTP Request for plain calls. For a local server needing a header token, a WebView XMLHttpRequest triggers a CORS preflight: use `shell()` + `nc` with the body in a file, and parse replies with `\r?\n\r?\n`. Never put a token in the task: read it from a file at run time, or let a Termux script make the call.

**Termux and Claude agents**
Start Termux scripts with RUN_COMMAND from a JavaScriptlet:
```
sendIntent('com.termux.RUN_COMMAND', 'service', 'com.termux',
  'com.termux.app.RunCommandService', 'none', '', '',
  ['com.termux.RUN_COMMAND_PATH:/data/data/com.termux/files/home/.termux/tasker/SCRIPT',
   'com.termux.RUN_COMMAND_STDIN:' + text,
   'com.termux.RUN_COMMAND_BACKGROUND:true']);
```
User text goes on stdin, never on a command line. Requirements: Tasker holds com.termux.permission.RUN_COMMAND, Termux has `allow-external-apps = true` (then `termux-reload-settings`). A Claude Code agent is one such script (`agent-<name>` -> claude-agent -> ssh into the PRoot -> `claude --agent <name> -p`); its answer comes back as a notification, not a return value. Details: termux-proot-bridge.

**Errors**
- Set "Continue Task After Error" only on actions whose failure you handle, and check %err / %errmsg right after them.
- Every exit path gives feedback: flash or notification on failure, with what to check.
- A task started by run_tasker_task gets no %par values and runs only after the user confirms; design it to ask or to read its input.

## Deliver
1. The action list: # | Action (code) | Arguments | Condition | Continue after error | Why.
2. The JavaScriptlet code in full, for each JS action.
3. Collision handling and priority for the task, and who calls it.
4. Delivery: Python using the build-claude-*.py helpers that emits a .prj.xml, then `tasker-edit.py edit --add-tasks FILE.prj.xml PROJECT --dry-run`, the same without --dry-run, and `push` (see tasker-direct-edit); or, for a new project, Tasker's importer: `source /root/phone/tasker/tasker-import.sh; tasker_import FILE NAME.prj.xml` (the user taps YES). Direct config writes (`push`, `restore`, `tile`, which use su over adb) run only in an interactive session with the user present and after their yes to the exact change. Headless, agent-started or Tasker-started runs (PHONE_SCREEN_LOCK=held, or no user in the loop) stop and return the commands as "Not done".
5. A test: how to run it alone (play button or run_tasker_task) and what output proves each branch.
